item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, in a king's frontier fortress there is a high, wide wall, with a coating of plaster on the outside, to protect those…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, in a king's frontier fortress there is a high, wide wall, with a coating of plaster on the outside, to protect those inside the fortress and to keep out those outside. So too, bhikkhus, a noble disciple has wisdom, possessing wisdom that penetrates arising and passing away, with the noble penetration leading to the complete destruction of suffering. Using wisdom as the plaster coating, bhikkhus, the noble disciple abandons the unwholesome, develops the wholesome, abandons what is blameworthy, develops what is blameless, and keeps himself pure. With this seventh excellent quality he is accomplished.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.67

item.title: Poṭṭhapāda, what are the teachings that I have declared and explained definitively? 'This is suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This…
item.description:
Poṭṭhapāda, what are the teachings that I have declared and explained definitively? 'This is suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This is the origin of suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This is the cessation of suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively. 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,' Poṭṭhapāda, that is a teaching I have declared definitively.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 9 – Poṭṭhapādasutta

item.title: Those who are excessively attached, Confused about things, Led astray by various sects, They sleep on and on, They are not awake. Now indeed it…
item.description:
Those who are excessively attached,
Confused about things,
Led astray by various sects,
They sleep on and on,
They are not awake.
Now indeed it is time
For them to awaken.
( Blessed One ):
Those who are not excessively attached,
Not confused about things,
Not led astray by various sects,
They have attained perfect enlightenment.
They fully understand perfectly,
On the uneven path,
They walk evenly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.8

item.title: - What binds the world? By taming what is one freed? By abandoning what thing Are all bonds cut? - Desire binds the world, By…
item.description:
- What binds the world?
By taming what is one freed?
By abandoning what thing
Are all bonds cut?
- Desire binds the world,
By taming desire one is freed,
By abandoning desire
Are all bonds cut.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.69

item.title: Time passes silently, Nights and days move quickly, Youth abandons us, One by one. Those who contemplate this fear of death, Should do meritorious deeds…
item.description:
Time passes silently,
Nights and days move quickly,
Youth abandons us,
One by one.
Those who contemplate this fear of death,
Should do meritorious deeds
That bring happiness.

( Blessed One ):
Time passes silently,
Nights and days move quickly,
Youth abandons us,
One by one.
Those who contemplate this fear of death,
Should abandon worldly gains,
Attain true peace.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.27

item.title: He avoids wrong livelihood such as: consulting mirrors, consulting female mediums, consulting devas for signs of good or evil, worshipping the sun, worshipping the earth,…
item.description:
He avoids wrong livelihood such as: consulting mirrors, consulting female mediums, consulting devas for signs of good or evil, worshipping the sun, worshipping the earth, spitting fire, invoking the goddess of fortune, using spells for good luck or causing misfortune. Such is his virtue in terms of moral discipline.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: Great king, just as a bird, wherever it flies, carries its two wings with it; so too, great king, the bhikkhu is content with a…
item.description:
Great king, just as a bird, wherever it flies, carries its two wings with it; so too, great king, the bhikkhu is content with a robe to protect his body and almsfood to sustain his stomach, and wherever he goes, he takes only these. Thus, great king, the bhikkhu is content.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: Whenever, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus dwell in harmony, rejoicing, without dispute, like milk mixed with water, looking at one another with loving eyes — at that…
item.description:
Whenever, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus dwell in harmony, rejoicing, without dispute, like milk mixed with water, looking at one another with loving eyes — at that time, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus generate much merit; at that time, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus dwell in the Brahma-state. That is, for one who rejoices with mind-liberation connected to happiness, happiness arises; for one with happiness, the body becomes tranquil; with a tranquil body, he feels pleasant feeling; for one feeling pleasant feeling, the mind becomes concentrated.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.95

item.title: Just as, Rādha, young boys or young girls play with sandcastles. As long as they are not free from lust, desire, love, thirst, passion, and…
item.description:
Just as, Rādha, young boys or young girls play with sandcastles. As long as they are not free from lust, desire, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they still have fun with them, play with them, treasure them, and delight in them. But when those boys or girls become free from lust, desire, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, then they break them apart, smash them, demolish them, and do not play with them. So too, Rādha, break apart, smash, demolish, and do not play with form; direct your mind to the destruction of craving for form. The destruction of craving, Rādha, is Nibbāna.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.2

item.title: Ānanda, those who, after my passing, are islands unto themselves, refuges unto themselves, with no other refuge; have the Dhamma as their island, the Dhamma…
item.description:
Ānanda, those who, after my passing, are islands unto themselves, refuges unto themselves, with no other refuge; have the Dhamma as their island, the Dhamma as their refuge, with no other refuge — those, Ānanda, will be the foremost among my bhikkhus, if they are eager to learn.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta
